881.text: Even shade or water becomes harmful if it causes illness; close relationships are no good when they repeatedly cause pain. For example, a familiar group is not a healthy one if its members constantly undermine you.

882.text: An open enemy is easier to guard against than someone who acts like a friend while secretly wishing you harm. For example, a clear competitor is safer to deal with than a partner who quietly misuses shared information.

883.text: Be alert to hostility within your own group, because it can destroy the group in a weak moment like a tool cutting a clay pot. For example, hidden factions can break a team apart when an urgent crisis arrives.

884.text: Hidden resentment in a person's mind can create many troubles and turn members of the same circle against one another. For example, an unspoken grudge in a family can spread until relatives stop supporting each other.

885.text: When serious hostility appears among relatives or close allies, it can bring many forms of harm, even lasting damage. For example, a bitter dispute over an inheritance can hurt an entire family.

886.text: When people who should stand together turn against one another, avoiding collapse becomes very difficult. For example, an organization divided by internal feuds may fail before any outside competitor defeats it.

887.text: A family or team with hidden hostility may look united outside, but it is not truly joined within. For example, coworkers can smile in a meeting while quietly working against one another.

888.text: Internal hostility steadily wears down a group's strength, just as filing wears away iron. For example, constant mistrust can slowly drain a company's best people and ideas.

889.text: Even a tiny hidden resentment can contain the power to cause great destruction. For example, a small rumor left unanswered can grow into a serious split among friends.

890.text: Living with people who do not share goodwill is like sharing a small hut with a snake: every moment feels unsafe. For example, roommates who secretly resent one another cannot relax at home.

891.text: The best protection is not to underestimate the strength of people who can carry a task through. For example, dismissing a capable coworker can leave you unprepared when that person takes decisive action.

892.text: Treat capable and respected people with care, because disregarding them can bring lasting trouble. For example, insulting a trusted mentor may close doors that an apology cannot easily reopen.

893.text: If someone wants ruin, they can ignore good advice and offend people who have the power to strike back. For example, a manager who breaks every rule and humiliates a capable team invites a serious downfall.

894.text: A weak person harming a strong one is like calling destruction to come by waving it closer. For example, posting a reckless accusation against a powerful organization can create consequences the poster cannot handle.

895.text: Those who anger a cruel and powerful ruler may find no safe place, wherever they go. For example, a worker under an abusive authority may need careful protection before leaving for another place.

896.text: A person may survive being burned by fire, but grave disrespect toward someone with great power may leave no safe escape. For example, do not casually provoke a powerful authority when a serious dispute can be resolved lawfully.

897.text: Wealth, comfort, and strong institutions mean little if honorable and capable people turn against you. For example, a wealthy leader can still lose everything after betraying the people who made the work possible.

898.text: Even people who seem firmly established can fall, along with their households or organizations, when powerful and respected people resolve to oppose them. For example, a corrupt company may collapse after its strongest partners unite against it.

899.text: When people committed to high principles rise against injustice, even a ruler can lose power and fall. For example, a government that ignores peaceful calls for fairness may lose public trust and authority.

900.text: Even with many resources and powerful allies, no one is safe from the anger of noble people whose integrity is great. For example, a well-connected official can still face ruin after seriously betraying a trusted community.

901.text: The verse warns against letting excessive attachment to a spouse replace duty and responsible purpose. For example, someone may skip an important community task just to avoid a partner’s displeasure.

902.text: A person who neglects responsibility and blindly follows a spouse can turn even great wealth into a source of shame. For example, a wealthy person may misuse their position to please a partner and lose others’ respect.

903.text: Someone who gives up their judgment out of fear at home may feel ashamed among good people. For example, they may stay silent when a partner asks them to act unfairly, then regret it around honest friends.

904.text: A person ruled by fear at home may never show courage or earn respect through action. For example, they may avoid leading a needed project because they fear their partner’s reaction.

905.text: If fear of a spouse controls someone, it can keep them from doing even good things for deserving people. For example, they may refuse to help a needy friend because their partner might object.

906.text: Even a person living in comfort and luxury lacks true dignity if fear makes them surrender their judgment. For example, a successful professional may still be unable to make an honest choice without permission.

907.text: The verse praises a woman’s self-respect above a man’s shameless dependence on a spouse’s every command. For example, staying honest under pressure shows more character than using status to please someone.

908.text: People who blindly follow a partner’s wishes may neglect friends in need and fail to do what is right. For example, they may cancel a promise to help a friend because their partner wants their time elsewhere.

909.text: When someone surrenders judgment to a partner’s commands, they may neglect virtue, responsible work, and healthy enjoyment. For example, they may abandon volunteering, career duties, and balanced recreation simply to avoid disagreement at home.

910.text: People with clear thinking, inner strength, and stable means do not lose themselves in blind dependence on a spouse. For example, they can love their partner while still making thoughtful, responsible decisions.

911.text: Sweet words offered only for money eventually bring sorrow. For example, someone who mistakes flattering messages for genuine affection and keeps paying may end up hurt and in debt.

912.text: Do not trust affection that appears only after someone measures what you can pay. For example, a person who keeps spending on someone who flatters them for gifts may find the relationship disappears when the money runs out.

913.text: An embrace offered only for money is empty, like holding a stranger’s corpse in the dark. For example, a person may feel deeply lonely after paying for attention that was never sincere.

914.text: Those who seek the wealth of compassion should not chase intimacy based only on money. For example, someone who values genuine relationships will step away from attention that depends entirely on expensive gifts.

915.text: A person with sound judgment does not lose themselves in pleasures offered indiscriminately to anyone who pays. For example, they choose relationships built on trust instead of chasing attention available only through spending.

916.text: People who protect their good character avoid intimacy sold as a boast or a service to every payer. For example, someone who wants a respected reputation will not trade their values for temporary attention.

917.text: People who cannot govern their desires may pursue someone whose body is present while their heart seeks other things. For example, a lonely person may mistake paid attention for love and ignore the lack of genuine care.

918.text: Without discernment, a deceitful person’s embrace can feel irresistible but lead to ruin. For example, someone who ignores warning signs may be drawn into a relationship that drains their money and trust.

919.text: Chasing a relationship with no moral boundaries can become a trap for people who ignore its consequences. For example, someone may keep returning to a costly affair until debt, shame, and isolation take over.

920.text: Deceitful relationships, alcohol, and gambling often gather around people who have lost their good fortune and self-control. For example, someone who spends nights drinking, betting, and chasing paid attention may quickly lose money and stability.

921.text: Those who constantly crave alcohol lose both their good name and the respect that makes others take them seriously. For example, a talented worker may be passed over for responsibility after repeatedly arriving drunk or unreliable.

922.text: Anyone who wants the respect of wise and honorable people should stay away from alcohol. For example, a student who wants teachers and future employers to trust them protects that reputation by refusing a drink that could impair judgment.

923.text: If drunkenness is painful for a mother to witness, it will be even more shameful before wise and honorable people. For example, if a parent cannot bear to see their child intoxicated, that child should understand how the behavior affects mentors and family.

924.text: Heavy drinking drives away modesty and self-respect. For example, someone who becomes reckless at parties may say or do things they would never accept when sober.

925.text: Paying to lose awareness of yourself is a foolish bargain. For example, buying alcohol to escape stress can leave a person unable to control their words, choices, or safety.

926.text: A person who repeatedly drinks is like someone taking poison: both surrender their clear awareness. For example, regular heavy drinking can damage health and make ordinary life feel as if the person is barely present.

927.text: Even secret drinking is rarely secret for long; signs of intoxication invite ridicule from those nearby. For example, a student who hides alcohol use may still be exposed by slurred speech and unsteady behavior.

928.text: A drunkard should not claim never to drink, because intoxication can reveal what they tried to hide. For example, someone who denies drinking may confess or behave recklessly once they lose control.

929.text: Reasoning with someone who is deeply drunk is as useless as searching underwater for a drowned person with a torch. For example, wait until a drunk friend is sober before discussing their dangerous choices.

930.text: When a sober drinker sees another person staggering drunk, they should remember that alcohol can make them look the same. For example, watching a friend embarrass themselves at a party should be a warning, not an invitation to repeat it.

931.text: Even a win does not make gambling safe; it can be the bait that hides the trap. For example, a lucky first bet may tempt someone to keep playing until losses exceed the original win.

932.text: A gambler who wins once but loses a hundred times cannot build a happy life through gambling. For example, using rent money to chase back losses can leave a family facing debt.

933.text: If someone keeps rolling dice for profit, their wealth and the means of earning it can pass into other people’s hands. For example, a person may sell savings or tools for betting and lose both money and livelihood.

934.text: Nothing creates poverty like gambling, which brings many troubles and destroys reputation. For example, repeated betting can lead to debt, broken promises, and lost trust at home and work.

935.text: People who refuse to give up gambling, the gambling venue, and the thrill of the game can end up with nothing. For example, someone may spend every payday at betting shops until bills and savings are gone.

936.text: Those trapped by gambling may neglect even their basic needs while suffering through constant worry. For example, a person chasing losses may skip meals or borrow money instead of caring for themselves.

937.text: Spending time gambling can destroy both inherited wealth and good character. For example, someone may waste family savings and start lying to relatives to keep playing.

938.text: Gambling can destroy money, encourage lies, weaken compassion, and bring misery. For example, a bettor who hides losses may deceive family members and become unable to help anyone else.

939.text: Gambling can drive away five essentials: clothing, wealth, food, reputation, and learning. For example, money spent on betting may replace tuition, groceries, and basic necessities.

940.text: The more a gambler loses, the more they may crave gambling—just as suffering can make a person cling more tightly to life. For example, after losing money, someone may keep betting to recover it and sink even deeper.

941.text: A healthy body depends on balance; excess or deficiency in its basic functions can cause illness. For example, constantly overeating or barely eating can both make someone sick.

942.text: When people eat only after earlier food has been digested, they may need little medicine. For example, waiting for real hunger instead of snacking nonstop helps a person avoid overloading their body.

943.text: After a meal is digested, eat only the amount the body needs; moderation helps preserve a long life. For example, stopping when comfortably satisfied rather than stuffed is a simple daily practice.

944.text: Notice when food has been digested, wait until you are truly hungry, and choose food that suits your body. For example, after a heavy meal, someone can wait rather than forcing another meal late at night.

945.text: Life faces fewer health troubles when we eat suitable food in moderation, even when we could eat more. For example, choosing a reasonable portion and stopping before overeating protects everyday well-being.

946.text: Moderation brings lasting comfort, while overeating gives illness a place to stay. For example, someone who eats slowly and stops at enough may feel well, while a person who keeps piling on food may suffer afterward.

947.text: Those who ignore their hunger and eat far too much invite countless illnesses. For example, regularly eating beyond fullness can lead to health problems instead of energy.

948.text: Good treatment begins by identifying the illness, finding its cause, and choosing a remedy that fits. For example, a doctor should investigate why a fever started before prescribing medicine, then treat it carefully.

949.text: A trained doctor should consider the patient’s condition, the illness, and the timing before treating it. For example, the right care for a child with a new infection may differ from treatment for an older adult with a long-term condition.

950.text: Successful treatment depends on four partners: the patient, the doctor, the medicine, and the caregiver who supports the process. For example, recovery is stronger when a patient follows instructions, the doctor treats wisely, the medicine is suitable, and family or staff provide care.

951.text: A truly honorable upbringing shows in consistency, honesty, and modest restraint—not merely in a family name. For example, a student who admits a mistake instead of changing their story shows this steady character.

952.text: Good character stays rooted in decent conduct, truthfulness, and modesty, whatever a person's status. For example, a team member who tells the truth and accepts correction earns trust more than someone who only claims a respected background.

953.text: A good person welcomes others, shares what they can, speaks kindly, and avoids insulting people. For example, a student who includes a new classmate and shares their notes shows all four qualities.

954.text: Even great wealth is not worth gaining through an act that brings shame on one's family or principles. For example, refusing to cheat for a profitable contract protects a reputation that money cannot restore.

955.text: Hard times may reduce what a generous person can give, but they need not destroy the wish to help. For example, someone with little money may still share a meal or offer practical help to a neighbor.

956.text: People who value their good name do not use deceit or harmful shortcuts, even when life becomes difficult. For example, a job seeker facing hardship should not invent qualifications to get hired.

957.text: A fault in a respected person is noticed as clearly as a mark on the moon. For example, a small dishonest act by a trusted leader may attract more attention than the same act by a stranger.

958.text: Kindness is so central to good character that its absence makes people question every claim of good upbringing. For example, a talented person who treats service workers coldly may lose respect despite their success.

959.text: A person's words often reveal their upbringing just as a crop reveals its soil. For example, the way an applicant speaks to everyone during an interview can show whether they have learned respect.

960.text: Modesty helps a person earn a good name, and humility toward everyone preserves lasting honor. For example, a popular student who treats classmates and staff with equal respect becomes respected for the right reasons.

961.text: Do not choose an act that destroys your honor, even when it seems urgently necessary. For example, a business should seek a lawful solution rather than accept a corrupt deal just to avoid a short-term loss.

962.text: People who want lasting respect will not commit a dishonorable act merely to win attention or fame. For example, an athlete who refuses performance-enhancing drugs protects both the achievement and the honor behind it.

963.text: Success calls for humility, while hardship calls for dignity and self-respect. For example, a newly promoted manager should stay approachable, and after losing the job should not surrender to humiliation.

964.text: When someone abandons a respected position and its principles, their former standing falls away like hair from the head. For example, a trusted official who sells decisions for approval can quickly lose the respect once earned.

965.text: Even a person who seems as firm as a mountain can fall through one small, degrading act. For example, a respected leader may damage years of trust with one cruel public insult.

966.text: Following people who constantly insult you may preserve a few comforts, but it brings neither honor nor lasting good. For example, someone trapped under a humiliating boss should look for a safe, dignified way to move on rather than accept abuse as a lifestyle.

967.text: It is better to leave a situation with self-respect than to survive by continually chasing someone who despises you. For example, choosing modest honest work can be better than keeping a lucrative role under a person who deliberately humiliates you.

968.text: Keeping the body alive is not a real remedy if doing so requires surrendering every principle and one's dignity. For example, an employee should seek help or another job rather than sign a serious lie that permanently stains their integrity.

969.text: The image of the animal that cannot live without its coat shows how deeply honor can matter to a proud and principled person. For example, someone may give up comfort and leave rather than accept a public demand to betray what they believe is right.

970.text: The world continues to honor people who would rather leave an unjust situation than live by humiliation. For example, a whistleblower who gives up a promotion to report serious wrongdoing may be remembered for courage.

971.text: Courage and the wish to achieve something worthwhile give life its light; giving up all effort makes life feel empty. For example, a young adult who keeps learning after repeated failures is living with this kind of inner drive.

972.text: Everyone is equal by birth; differences in achievement come from the quality of what people do. For example, a person's background does not decide their worth—skill, effort, and helpful actions do.

973.text: A high title cannot make a cruel person noble, and a modest position cannot make a good person inferior. For example, an honest cleaner may show more greatness than an executive who abuses power.

974.text: True greatness comes from guarding one's conduct and staying faithful to good principles. For example, a person who keeps clear boundaries and remains loyal despite tempting pressure protects their honor.

975.text: A truly capable person can complete difficult work through the proper method, even under pressure. For example, a good emergency team stays organized and solves a dangerous problem instead of taking reckless shortcuts.

976.text: Small-minded people do not value the chance to learn from admirable and capable people. For example, a student who rejects every helpful mentor misses the growth that comes from good guidance.

977.text: Wealth, education, or authority can produce arrogance when they are placed in the hands of someone without good character. For example, a newly promoted manager may start ordering people around simply because the title makes them feel superior.

978.text: Greatness is shown by steady humility, while smallness appears when someone keeps praising themselves. For example, a team leader who credits the whole group is greater than one who claims every success alone.

979.text: Real greatness means having reasons to boast but choosing not to; smallness is boasting without good reason. For example, a capable volunteer quietly helping others shows more greatness than someone making loud claims about minor favors.

980.text: A generous person protects others from needless embarrassment, while a petty person points out every fault. For example, a thoughtful colleague corrects a mistake privately instead of exposing it in a group chat—without hiding serious harm.

981.text: People who understand their duties and practice excellence come to see good actions as a natural responsibility. For example, a dependable volunteer does not wait for praise before completing an important task.

982.text: For a truly good person, character is the real beauty; appearance and other pleasures are secondary. For example, when choosing a friend, trustworthiness and kindness matter more than fashionable clothes.

983.text: Love, modesty about wrongdoing, generosity, compassion, and truthfulness are the five supports of strong character. For example, a reliable teammate cares about the group, shares credit, admits mistakes, and speaks honestly.

984.text: Self-discipline is grounded in refusing to harm living beings, and true goodness includes not spreading other people's faults. For example, a mature person avoids retaliation and does not forward a private mistake as gossip.

985.text: The strongest person is often the one who can act with humility; that attitude can turn opponents into partners. For example, a manager who listens respectfully to a critic may resolve a conflict better than one who relies on authority.

986.text: A person's character is tested by whether they can accept defeat, even from someone less experienced or less powerful. For example, a senior player who congratulates a junior teammate after losing shows real maturity.

987.text: Goodness has little value if it cannot respond kindly even to someone who has caused pain. For example, after a rude classmate asks for help, you can assist without excusing the rudeness or allowing further mistreatment.

988.text: Poverty is not disgraceful when a person possesses strong character and self-respect. For example, a student from a struggling family may lack expensive things yet be generous, honest, and dependable.

989.text: People of lasting character remain steady even when times, fashions, and pressures change. For example, a student who refuses to cheat when everyone else does keeps the same standards under pressure.

990.text: If trustworthy and principled people lose their character, society loses the support that holds it together. For example, a community can quickly fall into distrust when its leaders stop keeping promises and acting fairly.

991.text: Being approachable to everyone makes it easier to develop genuine good character. For example, a new coworker who welcomes questions and speaks simply helps others feel respected and builds better relationships.

992.text: Kindness and the respectful conduct associated with good upbringing together form proper behavior toward others. For example, a gracious host makes every guest feel welcome, whatever their wealth or position.

993.text: Shared bodies or backgrounds do not make people truly alike; shared good qualities do. For example, a diverse team becomes a real community when its members show fairness, care, and honesty toward one another.

994.text: The world praises people whose fairness and generosity make them genuinely useful to others. For example, a neighbor who organizes a fair food drive earns respect because their actions help the whole community.

995.text: Mockery can hurt even when it is called a joke, so mature people remain respectful even with rivals. For example, good sportsmanship means competing fiercely without humiliating the other team.

996.text: Everyday life depends on people who practice decency and trustworthiness. For example, honest teachers, shopkeepers, and neighbors make a community work; without them, suspicion would replace cooperation.

997.text: A person may have a brilliant mind, but without human kindness they act like a sharp tool with no life in it. For example, a gifted programmer who humiliates everyone around them has skill but lacks true humanity.

998.text: Even toward people who dislike or harm us, we should keep our own decency while maintaining sensible boundaries. For example, replying calmly to a hostile email protects your dignity better than returning the insult.

999.text: People who cannot share joy or connect with others may feel that the whole world is dark, even in good times. For example, an isolated student may begin to feel better after joining a welcoming club and making friends.

1000.text: Wealth gained by someone without goodness can become harmful, like pure milk spoiled by a dirty vessel. For example, a rich business that exploits workers may have money but turns its wealth into a source of harm rather than benefit.

1001.text: A person who piles up wealth but never uses it or shares it gains no real benefit from it. For example, saving every cent while never helping your family or enjoying a simple life leaves the fortune unused.

1002.text: Wealth can provide many comforts, but clinging to it and refusing to share it is a form of delusion that degrades a person's life. For example, someone who has plenty but will not help a neighbor lets greed rule them.

1003.text: People who care only about increasing their wealth and not about earning a good name become a burden to the world. For example, a business owner who profits greatly but never treats workers or customers fairly leaves no respected legacy.

1004.text: A person whom nobody loves because they never help anyone has little to look forward to leaving behind. For example, a miser may own a great deal, yet no one remembers them with gratitude after they are gone.

1005.text: If someone neither shares their wealth nor allows themselves to enjoy it, even millions are as useless as having nothing. For example, money locked away forever cannot feed a family, support a cause, or bring its owner any honest joy.

1006.text: Wealth becomes a kind of illness when its owner neither enjoys it nor uses it to help deserving people. For example, a person who hoards savings while refusing needed medical help to a dependent lets the fortune control them.

1007.text: Wealth that never helps people in need is like a beautiful opportunity kept locked away until its value is lost. For example, a well-funded scholarship that is never offered cannot change a student's life.

1008.text: The wealth of a disliked person is like poisonous fruit growing in the middle of a town: it may look plentiful, but people cannot safely benefit from it. For example, money built by exploiting workers brings fear rather than trust.

1009.text: Wealth earned without love, self-care, or concern for what is right will eventually be enjoyed by someone else. For example, an owner who sacrifices every relationship and acts dishonestly may leave the fortune to strangers when others take over.

1010.text: A short period of hardship for a generous and respected person is like a rain cloud that is briefly empty. For example, a community donor may face a temporary setback without losing the goodwill built through years of helping others.

1011.text: True modesty is feeling shame about doing wrong, not merely feeling shy. For example, a student who admits copying an answer and makes amends shows real modesty.

1012.text: Food, clothing, and other needs are common to everyone; what especially marks a good person is the modesty that keeps them from shameful acts. For example, someone may dress like everyone else but stand out by refusing to cheat.

1013.text: Just as the body gives life a home, modesty gives a person's excellence its inner support. For example, a talented leader who still feels responsible after hurting someone has character, not just ability.

1014.text: Modesty is an ornament of the noble; without it, their proud behavior becomes painful for everyone around them. For example, a successful manager who boasts after causing harm makes authority feel like arrogance.

1015.text: People who feel shame not only for their own wrongdoing but also for harm done to others become a true home for modesty. For example, a teammate who speaks up when someone is mocked shows concern beyond personal reputation.

1016.text: People of true greatness use modesty and self-restraint as their protection, rather than relying on wealth or status. For example, a powerful employee who refuses a corrupt shortcut is safer in the long run because their principles guard them.

1017.text: Those who deeply value modesty would rather accept a serious loss than protect themselves through a shameful act. For example, a student may give up an unfair advantage rather than win by cheating.

1018.text: When someone does what decent people would be ashamed of and feels no shame, virtue has effectively left them. For example, sharing a private photo to embarrass someone and laughing about it shows this loss of conscience.

1019.text: Breaking one's principles can disgrace a family, but living without shame can destroy one's own character and well-being. For example, repeated dishonest deals may damage both a family's name and the person's future.

1020.text: Someone without modesty or conscience moves through life like a puppet pulled by strings. For example, a person who joins in bullying just to win online approval is being controlled by the crowd rather than guided by judgment.

1021.text: There is no greater honor than deciding not to give up while carrying out one's responsibilities to family and community. For example, a parent who keeps working and learning through setbacks shows this steady greatness.

1022.text: A family or community grows through continued effort joined with sound knowledge and good judgment. For example, a parent who learns new skills and plans finances carefully can create better opportunities for the next generation.

1023.text: When someone firmly commits to uplifting their family or community, help and opportunities often seem to come forward to meet that effort. For example, a person who starts a useful local project may find neighbors and mentors ready to help.

1024.text: People who act promptly to improve their family's future often succeed without endless hesitation. For example, someone who begins training for a better job now is more likely to progress than someone who keeps waiting for the perfect time.

1025.text: People are drawn to someone who improves their family or community without using dishonest means. For example, an honest small-business owner earns loyal friends because success is joined with trust.

1026.text: True strength is taking responsibility for one's family and becoming a capable source of support, not simply claiming authority. For example, an older sibling who organizes help and protects younger family members shows this strength.

1027.text: Just as the bravest soldiers carry the hardest duties in battle, the most capable people must carry responsibility in a family or community. For example, during a crisis, the person with the right skills may need to coordinate help for everyone.

1028.text: Those working to improve their family's life cannot wait for a special season; laziness and wounded pride only make things worse. For example, delaying a job application because the work seems beneath you can leave the whole household struggling longer.

1029.text: A person who works to protect a family from harm may face hardship, but they are not meant only to suffer. For example, a caregiver may endure exhausting days while also finding support and relief for the people they protect.

1030.text: A family without someone able to support it in hard times can fall as quickly as a tree struck at its base. For example, when no one steps forward after a job loss, bills and problems can bring the household down.

1031.text: Farming is demanding, yet it is among the most important kinds of work because every other occupation depends on food from the land. For example, every meal eaten by an office worker or student begins with a farmer's labor.

1032.text: Farmers are a support for the whole world because they sustain people in every other line of work. For example, teachers, builders, and software workers can do their jobs only because someone grows their food.

1033.text: The verse praises those who live by farming as independent providers; others depend on what farmers produce. For example, a family that grows its own food contributes something essential instead of relying entirely on others for it.

1034.text: When farmers create plenty, they give strength and influence to the rulers and communities that depend on them. For example, a region with reliable harvests can support public services and remain strong in difficult times.

1035.text: People who live by their own work do not need to beg, and they can still share something with those who ask for help. For example, a day laborer may offer part of a meal to someone hungry, even without having much.

1036.text: If farmers stop working, even people who have renounced ordinary possessions cannot survive. For example, a retreat or monastery still depends on farmers to provide the food its residents eat.

1037.text: Careful, repeated preparation of the soil can make a crop thrive with little extra fertilizer. For example, a gardener who loosens and dries the soil properly may need fewer added materials later.

1038.text: Preparing and enriching the soil matters more than simply ploughing; after weeds are removed, protecting the crop matters even more than watering it. For example, a gardener who guards young plants from pests may save a harvest that regular watering alone would lose.

1039.text: Land needs its owner’s regular attention; when it is neglected, it stops rewarding the person who depends on it. For example, a garden left unchecked becomes dry and unproductive, just as a neglected responsibility slowly withdraws its benefits.

1040.text: The earth exposes the emptiness of someone who claims to have no means while refusing to make any effort. For example, a person who lets a usable garden or skill lie idle cannot fairly blame the opportunity for every hardship.

1041.text: Poverty itself is one of the deepest forms of suffering. For example, having to choose between food, rent, and medicine can make ordinary life painfully difficult.

1042.text: Severe poverty can take away both the comfort of the present and hope for a better future. For example, lacking money for food today may also prevent someone from getting healthcare or education tomorrow.

1043.text: When poverty creates desperate craving, it can damage a person's inherited dignity and the respect carried in their words. For example, constant financial pressure may push someone into humiliating demands or reckless deals.

1044.text: Even people from respected families may speak harshly when poverty wears down their patience and dignity. For example, someone overwhelmed by unpaid bills may say hurtful words they would normally avoid.

1045.text: Poverty often brings many other troubles along with it. For example, one missed rent payment can lead to debt, stress, missed classes, and damaged health.

1046.text: A poor person's wise and clearly expressed ideas may still be ignored simply because of their poverty. For example, a qualified applicant may be dismissed in an interview because of worn clothes rather than judged by their ability.

1047.text: When poverty is joined with conduct that abandons virtue, even close family may begin to treat a person like a stranger. For example, repeated dishonest choices made in desperation can break the trust of a person's own household.

1048.text: After poverty has hurt someone badly, they may fear that yesterday's suffering will return today. For example, someone who barely found food yesterday may check their money repeatedly, worried about tonight's meal.

1049.text: It may be possible to sleep in extreme heat, but poverty can make sleep itself hard to find. For example, worry about food, rent, or debt can keep a person awake long after the lights are out.

1050.text: The verse uses severe imagery for the crushing dependence of people who have no means to support themselves and must live on a neighbor's simplest food. For example, a family with no income may have to rely on others even for daily rice and salt, showing how harsh such poverty is.

1051.text: If you ask someone known to be able to help and they pretend they have nothing, the shame is theirs, not yours. When a capable sponsor refuses a deserving request while hiding their means, do not blame the person who asked.

1052.text: Asking for help can feel good when the person gives willingly and no one is hurt. A friend who lends notes without embarrassment makes receiving support a comfort, not a humiliation.

1053.text: There is dignity in asking an open-hearted person who understands their duty to help those in need. If a student honestly explains a hardship to a generous teacher, the request itself is honorable.

1054.text: Asking a person who never hides what they can give is almost like giving yourself, because the request lets their generosity do good. When someone gladly shares food with a hungry neighbor, accepting it completes the act of kindness.

1055.text: People ask because generous people exist who give without making them feel small. A family may seek help from a community kitchen because volunteers are ready to share what they have.

1056.text: Meeting people who do not hide their resources can lift the whole burden of poverty from those who ask. A fair relief fund that gives promptly can turn a desperate week into a manageable one.

1057.text: Those who give without insulting or mocking the needy bring real happiness to the person receiving help. Handing a meal to someone with a warm greeting is kinder than dropping it down with contempt.

1058.text: If no one ever needed help, the world's acts of giving would lose their purpose, like a puppet moving without a living hand. A donation matters because it reaches someone with a real need.

1059.text: Giving earns its honor because there are people who need and ask for help. A scholarship has meaning because a student is there to receive the chance.

1060.text: A person who asks should not grow angry when refused, since hardship may also prevent the other person from giving. If one shop cannot offer credit, accept the answer without abusing the shopkeeper.

1061.text: Even when generous people are ready to give, living without having to ask is far better. Building savings or earning your own income preserves independence.

1062.text: If people must beg simply to survive, the world has been made unjust; even its creator would deserve to feel that hardship. A society that leaves families dependent on handouts should question its own fairness.

1063.text: Nothing is more misguided than treating begging as the answer to poverty while refusing to seek work or other honest means. If someone can learn a skill but chooses only to demand support, they are avoiding the harder remedy.

1064.text: The dignity of refusing to beg, even when life offers no easy path, is beyond any wealth the world can offer. Someone who keeps seeking honest work through hardship shows a strength money cannot measure.

1065.text: Food can be plain porridge, but nothing tastes better than what your own effort has earned. A simple meal bought with wages can feel prouder than an expensive one received without effort.

1066.text: Even asking for water for a thirsty cow is described as painful to the tongue, because begging itself wounds dignity. When caring for an animal, ask respectfully but remember how vulnerable dependence feels.

1067.text: If you must ask for help, choose people who give openly, not those who hide what they have and resent the request. When seeking emergency aid, go to a transparent charity rather than someone who humiliates applicants.

1068.text: Begging is like an unsafe boat crossing poverty; it breaks apart when it hits the rock of refusal. Depending on one reluctant person for rent can leave you stranded, so build more reliable support where possible.

1069.text: Thinking about the pain of begging can soften the heart, but seeing someone hide help from a needy person can crush it. A community may feel compassion for a struggling family and anger at a wealthy neighbor who refuses aid out of spite.

1070.text: If a harsh refusal can crush the spirit of the person asking, what place is left for the life of the person who refuses while holding plenty? When a manager rejects an emergency request without even listening, the refusal says something about the manager too.

1071.text: Wicked people may look exactly like everyone else, but their lack of character sets them apart. A polite-looking classmate who secretly bullies others shows why appearance alone cannot prove goodness.

1072.text: People who know right from wrong may worry about living well, while the shameless seem carefree because they feel no such concern. Someone who cheats without remorse may look happier than the honest student who wrestles with conscience.

1073.text: Base people resemble gods only in one narrow sense: they do whatever they please without restraint. A person who ignores every rule may feel powerful, but that freedom is not the wisdom of a god.

1074.text: A bad person feels superior whenever they find someone even worse. Someone who lies about small things may boast that at least they have not committed a larger wrongdoing.

1075.text: The low behave well mainly because they fear punishment; sometimes they behave better when they expect a reward. An employee who follows safety rules only when a supervisor is watching has not developed true character.

1076.text: Mean people are like a loud drum: once they hear a secret, they carry its sound to everyone. If a friend shares a private problem, repeating it in a group turns trust into gossip.

1077.text: The mean will not share even leftovers with the vulnerable, but they may give something to a person strong enough to hurt them. Someone who tips a threatening bully but ignores a hungry worker reveals how fear, not generosity, guides them.

1078.text: Good people help when they hear a genuine need; mean people yield only after being pressured hard. A respected neighbor brings food when asked, while a selfish landlord acts only after repeated complaints.

1079.text: A mean person sees someone enjoying good food or clothing and looks for a fault to attack. If a classmate gets a new phone through honest work, jealousy may lead a petty person to spread rumors.

1080.text: When trouble comes, the mean may quickly sell their loyalty or freedom to escape it; that is what they are fit for. A person who abandons every principle as soon as money or pressure appears cannot be trusted in a crisis.

1081.text: On seeing her, the speaker cannot tell whether she is a divine being, a peacock, or a woman, so striking is her beauty. At a crowded event, one person's graceful presence can leave you momentarily lost for words.

1082.text: Her answering glance feels like a force that has returned with an entire army to overwhelm him. When someone you admire suddenly meets your eyes, one small look can make your nervousness feel enormous.

1083.text: He never understood what people meant by Death until he met the deadly power of this woman's fighting eyes. A confident glance from someone you like can feel so powerful that you suddenly forget what to say.

1084.text: Her gentle feminine nature seems at odds with eyes that look capable of taking away the life of anyone who meets them. A shy, kind person may still have an intense gaze that leaves an admirer speechless.

1085.text: Her look seems to hold all three powers at once: death, piercing eyes, and the timid beauty of a deer. One glance can feel frightening, attractive, and tender all at the same time.

1086.text: Her arched eyebrows soften the force of her eyes; if they covered them, he would not tremble so much. A quick smile or lowered brow from someone you like can make an intense moment feel safe.

1087.text: The cloth across her firm chest is compared with the cover placed over a powerful elephant's eyes; even her clothing seems full of force. At a cultural celebration, the way a traditional outfit moves can make a dancer's presence especially striking.

1088.text: The warrior's power that once frightened fearless enemies in battle collapses before the brightness of her forehead. Even a confident athlete or leader can become shy when someone they love appears.

1089.text: Her modesty and gentle, deer-like look are already ornaments; extra jewelry adds little. A simple outfit can be more beautiful when a person's grace and self-respect shine through.

1090.text: Wine gives pleasure only to the person who drinks it, but love can delight even through a single sight of the beloved. Seeing someone you care about across a room can brighten your mood before a word is spoken.

1091.text: Her eyes hold two looks: one causes the pain of love, and the other cures it. A worried glance followed by a warm smile from someone you love can turn anxiety into relief.

1092.text: A secret sideways glance can bring more pleasure than half the joy of physical closeness. At a gathering, one private look between two people can say more than a long conversation.

1093.text: She looks at him and then lowers her head in shyness; that small sign waters the growing plant of their love. When someone meets your eyes and then smiles shyly, the moment can deepen a new connection.

1094.text: When he looks at her, she looks at the ground; when he looks away, she watches him and smiles softly. A shy person may avoid eye contact during a conversation but smile when they think they are unobserved.

1095.text: She avoids looking straight at him, yet watches with a half-closed eye and smiles to herself. A playful side glance across a classroom can reveal affection without a direct confession.

1096.text: Even if she speaks as though they are strangers, her words soon show that no anger lies beneath them. A person who answers curtly but still checks that you are okay may be hiding affection rather than hostility.

1097.text: Brief sharp words and hostile-looking glances can be signs of lovers pretending to be strangers. Two people who tease each other in public may be protecting a private bond, not starting a real quarrel.

1098.text: When he looks at her, the tender smile she returns is a comforting sign. After a misunderstanding, a gentle smile from someone you care about can reassure you that the affection remains.

1099.text: Lovers may look at each other in public as if they were strangers. At a family gathering, two people in love might keep their faces neutral while sharing a private understanding.

1100.text: When two lovers' eyes agree completely, spoken words add nothing. A couple can understand reassurance, affection, or apology through one shared look before either speaks.

1101.text: The person you love can make every sense feel alive: sight, sound, taste, scent, and touch. After a difficult day, even a partner's welcoming smile, voice, and embrace can make the whole world feel warm again.

1102.text: Love can be both the wound and the cure. When someone's absence hurts, hearing their voice or making peace after a misunderstanding may bring relief in a way nothing else can.

1103.text: For someone deeply in love, resting beside a beloved can feel sweeter than any imagined heaven. After a long day, falling asleep peacefully next to the person you cherish may feel like the best place in the world.

1104.text: Love can feel like a strange fire: distance makes it burn, while closeness cools the pain. When a loved one stops replying, worry grows; a kind conversation can calm it at once.

1105.text: Being with the person you desire can bring the joy of receiving exactly what you hoped for. After waiting all week to see someone special, their simple hug can feel like the reward you had been longing for.

1106.text: A loving embrace can make a tired spirit feel young and renewed, as though it were made of nectar. After a frightening or exhausting day, a trusted person's hug can help someone feel alive again.

1107.text: The happiness of a loving embrace is compared with the joy of living in one's own home on honestly earned food shared with others. A peaceful home, fair work, and a caring partner can together bring a deep sense of contentment.

1108.text: For two people who truly love each other, an embrace with no space between them is especially sweet. When one partner is upset, holding each other close can offer comfort before either person finds the right words.

1109.text: Love includes small quarrels, understanding what went wrong, and finding happiness together again. For example, a couple may disagree, talk honestly, apologize, and feel even closer after making peace.

1110.text: The more deeply we know someone we love, the more we discover about our feelings, just as learning reveals how much we do not yet know. Each shared conversation can make affection feel fresh instead of ordinary.

1111.text: The beloved is said to be softer than the delicate anicham flower. It is a playful way of praising tenderness, like saying a loved one's gentle touch feels softer than anything else you have known.

1112.text: The speaker's heart mistakes ordinary flowers for the beloved's remarkable eyes, then feels confused when it looks at them. Seeing a flower that reminds someone of a loved one can suddenly bring that person to mind.

1113.text: The beloved is praised with many images at once: a tender shoot for her skin, pearls for her teeth, fragrance for her breath, and a spear for her dark, striking eyes. It captures how love makes every detail seem extraordinary.

1114.text: The blue lotus is imagined as lowering its head because it cannot match the beloved's eyes. When someone admires a friend's exceptional talent, even the usual standards of beauty may seem inadequate beside it.

1115.text: The beloved is so delicate that even an anicham flower becomes painful if its stem is left on. The exaggerated image humorously shows how a small careless detail can trouble someone very sensitive.

1116.text: The beloved's face shines so brightly that even the stars seem unable to tell it apart from the moon. When someone enters a dim room with a radiant smile, everyone's attention can turn toward them.

1117.text: The moon has visible marks, but the beloved's face is imagined as having none. This is the affectionate exaggeration of someone who sees no flaw at all in the person they love.

1118.text: The moon would be worthy of love only if it could shine like the beloved's face. When a familiar song reminds someone of a loved one, even the song feels special because of that association.

1119.text: The moon is teasingly told not to appear before everyone if it wants to resemble the beloved, because the beloved's beauty feels private and unmatched. A person may want to keep a precious moment with someone special just for themselves.

1120.text: Even an anicham flower or a swan feather would feel like a thorn to feet imagined this delicate. The image shows how love magnifies a beloved's gentleness beyond ordinary comparisons.

1121.text: The sweetness between loving partners is compared with milk mixed with honey, even in the smallest intimate detail. A gentle word from someone close can make an ordinary moment feel unexpectedly sweet.

1122.text: The bond between the lovers is like the union of body and soul: neither feels complete without the other. When two partners naturally share plans, worries, and joys, separation can feel like losing part of oneself.

1123.text: The speaker jokingly asks the image in his pupil to leave because there is no room for it; the beloved fills his sight and thoughts completely. Someone deeply in love may notice that every photo, song, or place brings the same person to mind.

1124.text: When the beloved is present, life feels alive; when she leaves, it feels like life itself has departed. After a loved one leaves for a long journey, an ordinary room can suddenly feel empty and lifeless.

1125.text: The speaker never needs to pause and remember the beloved because he has never forgotten her. When someone is constantly in your thoughts, even a reminder is unnecessary; their qualities are already present in your mind.

1126.text: The lover is imagined as living within the speaker's eyes, so gently that even blinking cannot hurt him. A cherished memory can stay quietly present through every moment without demanding attention.

1127.text: The speaker will not even apply eye makeup because the beloved is imagined as living inside the eyes and might be hidden. It playfully shows how completely a loved one occupies someone's attention.

1128.text: The lover is imagined as living inside the speaker's heart, so hot food seems capable of hurting him too. This humorous exaggeration expresses a closeness in which one person feels the other's pain as their own.

1129.text: The speaker refuses to blink because the lover seems to disappear whenever the eyes close, while outsiders wrongly call him uncaring. People who see only a brief absence may misjudge a relationship they do not understand.

1130.text: The lover is always happily present in the speaker's heart, even though the town assumes that distance means a lack of love. A couple living in different cities may remain deeply connected despite what others think.

1131.text: When love is blocked and the heart suffers, the traditional answer is to ride a palmyra horse, a public declaration of love. In the poem's world, someone who cannot win a beloved privately may boldly announce the love before the community.

1132.text: The pain of separation becomes so strong that the speaker is ready to set aside shame and make that public declaration. Someone who has endured a long silence may finally speak openly rather than continue hiding the hurt.

1133.text: The speaker once had modesty and self-control, but desperate love has driven him toward the palmyra horse, the public act of declaring his passion. A normally reserved person may behave boldly when unreturned love becomes unbearable.

1134.text: Strong desire is pictured as a flood that carries away the rafts of modesty and self-restraint. Someone who usually keeps calm may send an emotional message or make a public confession when feelings surge beyond control.

1135.text: The beloved has brought both the sadness that grows at evening and the desperate thought of riding the palmyra horse. Waiting alone at night for a reply can turn affection into restless sorrow and bold plans.

1136.text: The speaker cannot sleep and keeps thinking about making a public declaration of love. Anyone awake at midnight replaying a painful conversation may understand how longing can keep the mind from resting.

1137.text: The woman who endures even a sea of longing without making a public spectacle of it is praised as especially noble. The verse values her patience and restraint when private love brings intense pain.

1138.text: Love can break out of secrecy and become public before the lovers are ready, without caring how modest or private they are. A hidden relationship may become school or neighborhood gossip after one revealing glance.

1139.text: The speaker's love thinks no one knows about it, yet it seems to wander confused through every street. Feelings that someone tries to hide may still appear in their face, messages, or nervous behavior.

1140.text: People who have never felt this kind of suffering may laugh at the person who is struggling. Someone who has never faced heartbreak may joke about a friend's sadness instead of understanding it.

1141.text: Rumours about the lovers keep the speaker's hope and life from fading, while the people spreading them do not know why they matter. Even careless talk can give someone courage when it suggests that a difficult love may still succeed.

1142.text: The town does not understand the beloved's worth, yet its gossip accidentally helps the lovers by bringing their relationship into the open. A rumor meant as criticism can sometimes push families to acknowledge what was already true.

1143.text: The speaker welcomes a rumor known throughout the town because public talk makes an unrealized relationship feel almost achieved. When friends openly recognize two people's affection, it can feel like an important step toward being together.

1144.text: Gossip makes the speaker's passion grow stronger; without that outside talk, it would lose some of its force. The more classmates discuss a secret relationship, the more intensely the people involved may think about it.

1145.text: Each time the love becomes public, it feels more enjoyable, like a drink that seems sweeter with every happy taste. When a loved one's name is mentioned warmly among friends, the recognition can make the affection feel even more exciting.

1146.text: The lovers met for only one day, but the rumor spread as widely as the old image of a serpent seizing the moon in an eclipse. A brief conversation at an event can become the story everyone repeats by the next morning.

1147.text: The lovers' pain grows stronger through the town's gossip and the mother's angry words, just as a crop grows with manure and water. Opposition can sometimes deepen feelings instead of ending them.

1148.text: Trying to end love through gossip is like trying to put out a fire by pouring ghee on it: the attempt only feeds the flames. Public criticism may make two people think about each other even more.

1149.text: The person who promised not to leave has gone away and caused shame before others, so the speaker refuses to feel ashamed of their gossip too. After someone breaks a promise, the deeper wrong is the betrayal, not the comments made by onlookers.

1150.text: The town is spreading exactly the rumor the speaker hopes for, and the lover may agree when the time is right. When relatives begin speaking positively about a match, it can give someone hope that the relationship will be accepted.

1151.text: If you are staying, tell me plainly. If you must leave and return soon, tell that promise to those who may still be alive when you come back. When a partner says they will be away, the uncertainty can make every day feel unbearable.

1152.text: His look once made me happy, but now even being close to him hurts because I am already afraid of losing him. When someone you love is preparing to leave, a happy moment can be shadowed by worry.

1153.text: Even a wise lover may one day leave, so I cannot feel fully secure in his promise to stay. When plans change despite good intentions, trust can still feel fragile.

1154.text: He told me not to fear and promised he would not leave; if he goes, how can believing him be my fault? When someone breaks a reassuring promise, the person who trusted it is not to blame.

1155.text: If you want to protect my life, do not let my beloved leave. Once he goes, finding our way back to each other may be nearly impossible. A couple should face a difficult separation before it becomes permanent.

1156.text: If he is hard-hearted enough to announce that he is leaving, I should not expect him to return and show tenderness. When someone says goodbye without concern for your pain, holding on to hope can only hurt more.

1157.text: The bangles slipping from my thinning arm seem ready to tell everyone that my beloved plans to leave. When stress makes a bracelet loose, even a small change can reveal a hidden heartbreak.

1158.text: Living in a place where no one cares for you is painful, but being separated from the person you love is worse. Moving to a new city is hard; missing the one person who feels like home can be harder.

1159.text: Fire burns only when you touch it, but love's pain burns even when the beloved is far away. A person can be hurt by longing while sitting alone with no one near.

1160.text: Many people may agree to a painful separation, survive the grief, and keep living afterward—but I do not know how I could. When a partner leaves for work or duty, staying strong can feel possible for others and impossible for you.

1161.text: I try to hide this love-sickness, but it grows like a spring that rises the more water is drawn from it. The more I pretend I am fine after a breakup, the harder the feelings can return.

1162.text: I cannot hide this pain, yet I am too shy to tell the person who caused it. Sometimes you want to message someone who hurt you, but embarrassment stops you from saying how much you still care.

1163.text: Love and modesty hang on either side of my suffering body, with my life as the balancing pole. I want to tell my absent beloved how much I hurt, but shame holds my words back.

1164.text: The sea of longing surrounds me, but I have no safe boat to cross it. During a long separation, strong feelings can feel overwhelming when there is no comfort or reassurance.

1165.text: If he can bring sorrow into a friendship, what might he do if he became an enemy? Someone who causes pain even while close is especially hard to trust when conflict begins.

1166.text: Love's joy can be as vast as the sea, but when love turns into separation, its pain can be even greater. A happy relationship can make a breakup feel larger than anything you expected.

1167.text: I have tried to swim through this flood of longing but still cannot see its shore; even at midnight, I am alone. When everyone else is asleep and you are still waiting for someone, the night can feel endless.

1168.text: Night puts every living thing to sleep, yet I am its only companion. When the whole house is quiet and you alone are awake missing someone, the silence feels like company.

1169.text: These long nights are crueler than the distant beloved who causes my pain. When you keep checking the time for a message, one night can seem longer than the whole day.

1170.text: If my eyes could travel to my beloved as easily as my thoughts do, they would not have to swim through tears. When you cannot visit someone you miss, your mind goes there while your eyes remain stuck at home.

1171.text: My eyes first showed me the beloved who caused this unending pain, so why do they now weep and ask to see him again? It is like staring at an old photo that started the longing and then blaming the tears.

1172.text: My kohl-lined eyes looked at him without thinking about the consequences; why do they now suffer without admitting their part in my pain? A quick glance can begin feelings that are difficult to control later.

1173.text: My eyes rushed eagerly to see him, and now they are the ones crying. Their change is almost laughable. The same eyes that celebrated a meeting can make you cry when the person is gone.

1174.text: My painted eyes gave me a lasting love-sickness, and now their tears have dried up. After crying through a separation for so long, even the eyes that began it can grow tired.

1175.text: My eyes caused a longing larger than the sea, and now they cannot sleep because of it. After a late-night goodbye, the same eyes that sought out a loved one may stay awake until morning.

1176.text: The eyes that gave me this love-sickness are suffering from it too, and I am almost glad. When the same eyes that kept checking for a message finally swell from crying, it feels like a small kind of justice.

1177.text: May the eyes that once gazed at him with eager affection suffer until their tears run dry. The eyes that kept looking for an absent lover through the night seem to punish themselves.

1178.text: He may have loved me only with his words, not his heart, yet my eyes cannot rest without seeing him. Even when someone's promises felt shallow, missing them can still keep you awake.

1179.text: When he is away, my eyes cannot sleep; when he is here, they still cannot sleep, fearing his next departure. Waiting for someone and worrying about losing them can steal sleep either way.

1180.text: People here can easily discover our secret because eyes like mine beat it out like a drum. Even if you say nothing about a crush, tired, tearful eyes may tell everyone.

1181.text: I agreed to let the one I love leave; now that separation has made me pale, whom can I tell? Saying you are fine with a partner's decision can feel different once you are alone with its consequences.

1182.text: Paleness spreads over my body as though proud to say that my beloved caused it. When separation shows on your face, even your appearance seems to announce who you are missing.

1183.text: He took my beauty and shyness and left me love-sickness and pallor in return. After someone leaves, the sadness can change how you look and how freely you carry yourself.

1184.text: I think of him and speak only of his good qualities, yet this pallor has appeared anyway. Even when you remember someone fondly and say nothing bitter, missing them can still show on your face.

1185.text: Look there—my beloved is leaving; look here—paleness is already spreading over me. When a loved one walks away, the stress can show in your face before you have time to hide it.

1186.text: Just as darkness waits for a lamp to fade, paleness waits for my beloved's embrace to loosen. A small change in a close relationship can be enough for worry to appear.

1187.text: I was lying close to him, but moved only a little, and paleness rushed over me at once. After a warm goodbye, even a brief distance can suddenly make you feel the loss.

1188.text: People say only that she has grown pale; no one says that her beloved has left her. Others may notice the visible sadness while ignoring the separation that caused it.

1189.text: If the beloved who persuaded me to accept his departure is truly a good and caring person, let my body grow pale as it must. When you agree to a loved one's choice, you may still bear the physical cost of that separation.

1190.text: If no one blames the beloved who persuaded me to let him go, I would rather be known as the woman who turned pale. When people protect the person who left, even being known for the sadness feels preferable.

1191.text: Those who love each other in return receive love's sweetest fruit, free of the bitterness of one-sided longing. A relationship feels most fulfilling when the person you choose chooses you too.

1192.text: The beloved's timely affection is like rain to people whose lives depend on it. A caring message or visit at the right moment can give a strained relationship the strength to continue.

1193.text: The confidence that says ‘we will live happily’ belongs to those whose love is returned. When both partners still choose each other, even a difficult period feels survivable.

1194.text: A person may be admired by many, but feels no true blessing if the beloved they choose does not love them back. Praise from others cannot replace affection from the person who matters most.

1195.text: What can the person I love give me if they do not love me in return? A one-sided relationship cannot provide the comfort you hoped to receive.

1196.text: Love hurts when it rests on one side alone, like a kavadi carried with weight at only one end; it is joyful when both sides carry it. A relationship works best when both people make an effort.

1197.text: Does Love itself not see the pain and sorrow when it stands on only one side? When only one partner keeps reaching out, that person carries all the longing and change.

1198.text: No one is harder-hearted than a person who can go on living without even one kind word from the beloved they love. Going days without a caring message from someone important can make the silence feel cruel.

1199.text: Even if the person I love shows me no affection, anything said about him still sounds sweet to my ears. When you still care about someone, even a small mention of them can feel comforting.

1200.text: O my heart, if you are going to tell your deep pain to someone who does not care, you might as well try to fill the sea. When a person has stopped listening, seeking comfort from them can feel harder than an impossible task.

1201.text: Love can be sweeter than alcohol because its happiness can return whenever we remember it. A special moment with someone you love may still warm you long after the evening is over.

1202.text: Thinking about the person you love can make separation easier, so love feels sweet in every situation. When you miss someone who is away, rereading a kind message can bring comfort.

1203.text: A sneeze that almost comes but stops makes her wonder whether her beloved began thinking of her and then stopped. It is like seeing someone start typing a message, then watching the message disappear.

1204.text: Her beloved always lives in her heart, and she wonders whether she lives in his heart too. When you keep thinking about someone, you naturally hope the feeling is mutual.

1205.text: He has given her no place in his heart, yet he keeps returning to hers, so she asks whether he feels any shame. A person may try to move on, but reminders of someone who left can keep appearing in the mind.

1206.text: Memories of the days spent together are what keep her alive while they are apart. During a difficult separation, looking back at genuinely happy moments can give someone the strength to get through the day.

1207.text: Even remembering their past happiness makes her heart ache, but she cannot imagine forgetting it. An old photo may hurt because it brings back what was lost, yet deleting it can feel impossible.

1208.text: She can think of her beloved as much as she wants without angering him; that happiness itself is his gift to her. Rereading a loved one’s messages can still feel comforting, even when the person is far away.

1209.text: The person who once said they were one has now become so unkind that thinking about it slowly wears her down. Broken promises can hurt most when they once made a relationship feel completely secure.

1210.text: She asks the moon not to set, so its light can help her search for the beloved who has gone away. Someone waiting for a distant loved one may linger outside at night, hoping for one more glimpse or sign.

1211.text: A dream that brings a message from her beloved deserves a warm welcome. After missing someone for a long time, even a dream of talking with them can feel like a precious visit.

1212.text: If her eyes would only sleep as she asks, she could tell her beloved in a dream that she is still surviving. Sometimes a person falls asleep hoping a dream will let them say what they cannot say awake.

1213.text: Dreaming of the beloved who does not show affection while awake is what keeps her alive. After a long silence, even a dream of receiving a call from that person can briefly restore hope.

1214.text: Her dreams bring her the beloved who does not come to her in waking life, and that reunion gives her joy. When someone is absent, the mind may create the meeting that real life has denied.

1215.text: Seeing her beloved in real life was sweet then, and seeing him in a dream is just as sweet now. A cherished memory and a vivid dream can both make someone feel close to a loved one again.

1216.text: If waking life did not interrupt her dreams, the beloved who visits her there would never have to leave. An alarm ending a beautiful dream can feel like being separated from someone all over again.

1217.text: The beloved who gives her no affection while awake still appears in her dreams and causes pain, so she asks why. Dreaming about someone who will not answer your messages can reopen the hurt you tried to hide.

1218.text: In sleep he seems to rest on her shoulder, and when she wakes he quickly settles in her heart. After a vivid dream about someone you love, their presence can stay with you through the morning.

1219.text: People who never see their loved ones in dreams blame the man who does not visit her while she is awake. They judge the relationship from what they can see, not from the private comfort her dreams provide.

1220.text: The people around her say that her beloved has abandoned her because they do not know he still comes to her in dreams. Outsiders may see only distance, while a person’s inner life holds memories they cannot see.

1221.text: Evening is no longer a peaceful time; after her beloved’s departure, it feels like it destroys her. The hour that once marked the end of a good day can become the hardest time when someone is alone.

1222.text: She speaks to the dark evening as if it also suffers, asking whether its companion is as hard-hearted as hers. When loneliness settles in, even the dim sky can seem to share the pain of a deserted person.

1223.text: Evening once arrived with only a little unease, but now it returns with sorrow that grows stronger and makes life feel unbearable. Each sunset can deepen the ache of someone waiting for a loved one who is far away.

1224.text: Without her beloved, evening arrives like an enemy entering a place of slaughter. The quiet at sunset can feel frightening when an empty room brings back the fact that someone is gone.

1225.text: She wonders what kindness morning received and what offense she gave evening, since morning is bearable but evening brings pain. When missing someone, the day may pass calmly until dusk suddenly makes the loneliness sharp.

1226.text: Before her beloved left, she never knew that evening could be so painful. A familiar time of day can change completely after a breakup or a long separation.

1227.text: Her longing begins as a small feeling in the morning, grows through the day, and reaches its fullest strength by evening. Missing someone can build quietly during busy hours and become overwhelming when the day grows still.

1228.text: The shepherd’s flute once sounded pleasant, but now it announces the painful evening and feels like a weapon. A song that used to make someone happy can become painful when it is tied to a person who is gone.

1229.text: When evening clouds her mind, it seems as if the whole town has become confused and is suffering with her. Strong loneliness can color the streets, sounds, and faces around you with the same sadness you feel inside.

1230.text: Her life had endured, but evening makes her lose heart when she thinks of the beloved who left to pursue wealth. Waiting for a partner who is away working can feel especially heavy when the day ends without news.

1231.text: Her eyes weep for the beloved who has gone far away, losing their brightness and turning away from beautiful flowers. Deep sorrow can make even ordinary pleasures feel impossible to notice.

1232.text: Her pale, tearful eyes seem to reveal to everyone that the beloved she loves has not shown her kindness. Even when someone says nothing, tired eyes can show friends that something is wrong.

1233.text: The shoulders that once grew full with the joy of union have become thin, openly revealing the separation. Grief can show in a person’s appearance before they are ready to talk about it.

1234.text: After her companion leaves, her former beauty fades and her bracelets grow loose on her thinner arms. Long stress and sadness can affect the body as well as the heart.

1235.text: Her loosened bracelets and faded shoulders tell everyone how cruelly the beloved has left her. A person’s changed appearance can reveal neglect and heartbreak even when they try to hide both.

1236.text: She is hurt when people call her beloved cruel because her shoulders have grown thin and her bracelets have loosened. Even while suffering, she still loves him and does not want others to condemn him.

1237.text: She asks her heart whether telling the absent beloved about her fading body would bring it any real honour or relief. Writing one more message to someone who is not listening may only expose the pain without changing the situation.

1238.text: When the embrace loosens even slightly, the young woman’s forehead turns pale, as if she cannot bear the smallest separation. A brief goodbye can feel huge when two people are deeply attached.

1239.text: Even a breath of cool air slipping between the lovers during an embrace makes her large eyes lose their color. When someone is already anxious about separation, the smallest interruption can feel like abandonment.

1240.text: Her eyes seem troubled when they see the bright forehead become pale with longing. Noticing a loved one’s distress can make your own sadness feel heavier too.

1241.text: She asks her heart to find some remedy for a love-sickness that no ordinary medicine can cure. A person may try distractions and advice, yet still feel that only the absent loved one can ease the longing.

1242.text: Her heart suffers for someone who does not love her, and she calls that suffering foolish. Checking repeatedly for a reply from someone who has shown no care can keep the hurt alive.

1243.text: She asks why her heart stays and suffers over the person who caused the pain, since he has no compassion for her. Replaying conversations with someone who will not respond only deepens the wound.

1244.text: She begs her heart to take her eyes along when it goes to the beloved, because they ache to see him so fiercely. When the mind longs to visit someone, even the eyes seem restless for the sight.

1245.text: She asks whether she can give up loving a person simply because he does not return her love. Caring does not vanish on command, even when a relationship has become one-sided.

1246.text: Her heart pretends to stay angry, but it knows the beloved would quickly end the quarrel with affection. Someone may rehearse a serious complaint, then smile the moment the person they love walks in.
